title: Gassin, belvedere, ramparts and garden above the gulf
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Gassin is read through its height. Ramparts, garden, church and the broad view over the gulf give the village unusual density despite its tight footprint.
content:
In Gassin, everything begins with height. The village occupies little space, yet it opens very far. This tension between compact settlement and broad landscape gives the walk its strength.

Ramparts and edge lines

In Gassin, the edges matter as much as the centre. Ramparts, breaks in slope and facade points of support immediately convey the watch-post position of the village.

The garden and cultivation as an extension of the site

The walk is not only mineral. The remarkable garden, vines, olive trees and agricultural memory extend the reading of the heights. They show that Gassin is not detached from the ground despite its belvedere character.

A village to be read slowly

In Gassin, only a short distance is needed to change the angle. The point is therefore not to multiply kilometres, but to vary stops, framings and renewed views over the gulf and the peninsula.

This note extends the page Walking Through Gassin. To continue within the same cluster, it also helps to open Ramatuelle, a spiral village: how to walk through it without rushing across.
